QuestionStmt.S: Solubility of Ca₃(PO₄)₂ is 'S' mol dm⁻³. Find solubility product.

Solution.S:
The dissociation of Ca₃(PO₄)₂ is:

$$\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2 \rightleftharpoons 3\text{Ca}^{2+} + 2\text{PO}_4^{3-}$$

Let solubility be $S$ mol dm⁻³. Then:

$$[\text{Ca}^{2+}] = 3S, \quad [\text{PO}_4^{3-}] = 2S$$

Solubility product:

$$K_{sp} = [\text{Ca}^{2+}]^3 \times [\text{PO}_4^{3-}]^2 = (3S)^3 \times (2S)^2 = 27S^3 \times 4S^2 = 108S^5$$

Thus the correct option is B: $108S^5$.
